## Purpose
Implements the agent-composition UI surface: a modal/drawer for inspecting and configuring a single pipeline agent (`AgentCapabilitiesModal`), the per-agent system-prompt viewer/editor (`AgentPromptSection`), the skills/hooks attachment tab (`SkillsHooksTab`), and the live capability palette that lets a user browse and add registry capabilities to a workflow (`CapabilityPaletteSection`). It is the shared detail/config surface reused by the Library page, the Composer, and the workflow launch flow.

## Shape
- `getRole(agentId, pipelineType)` / `LOCKED_AGENT_IDS` / `REQUIRED_AGENT_IDS` — classifies an agent as locked/required/optional per pipeline; exported for reuse by the Composer's `AgentRow`.
- `AgentPromptSection` — collapsible viewer for an agent's base `AGENT.md` prompt plus an optional per-user override (edit/save/revert via `getAgentPrompt`/`saveAgentPromptOverride`/`deleteAgentPromptOverride`); a `surfaceOnly` flag strips the write affordances for read-only callers (e.g. the drawer Config tab).
- `AgentCapabilitiesModal` — the main 4-tab (Overview/Skills/Hooks/Config) inspector, renderable as a centered modal or a slide-in drawer (`asDrawer`); Config tab hosts `ConfigLeversFlat` for per-agent model/validator/gate/retry overrides, reported upward via `onSelectionsChange`.
- `SkillsHooksTab` — standalone skills/hooks browse-and-attach panel bound to `SkillsHooksContext`, reused by the Composer's "Skills & hooks" card.
- `CapabilityPaletteSection` — fetches the live `/api/capabilities` registry and renders every capability kind grouped and (for disallowed users) visibly locked.
- Several helpers (`getAgentInitials`, `PIPELINE_LABEL`, `getCapabilities`) are exported so the Composer reuses the exact same display logic instead of forking it.

## Why this shape
The file consolidates several agent-detail surfaces (modal, drawer, tabs, palette) that must stay visually and behaviorally identical across the Library, Composer, and launch-wizard entry points; functions are exported individually rather than split into separate files so those callers can reuse exact logic (role classification, initials, prompt section) without duplicating it — comments in the code explicitly flag this reuse intent (e.g. "EXPORTED (41-04)").
